newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila advertisers buck ABS-CBN rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Manila advertisers buck ABS-CBN rate hike.

text.p: A group of Philippine advertisers in ABS-CBN Broadcasting Corp, the country's biggest broadcasting company, has cancelled advertising slots to protest the network's proposed 22 percent advertising rate increase.

Philippine Association of National Advertisers (Pana) president Agapito Alcantara told Reuters on Wednesday that while the group objects to the 22 percent rate hike, it is amenable to a 15 percent increase. Pana has 302 members.

"We are waiting for them to call us; we did not want to post those telecast orders since it would mean we are agreeing to the new rates," Alcantara added. He said orders issued since Monday have been cancelled until the matter is resolved.
Some Pana member companies include stock market heavyweights San Miguel Corp, Petron Corp, Ayala Corp, Ayala Land Inc and the Philippine National Bank.
"Our members do not want to accept it. It's too high. We insist on a 15 percent increase," Alcantara said.
ABS-CBN said on Wednesday it would maintain the proposed 22 percent rate increase despite opposition.

"As of now, we are standing by our position of 22 percent. Most of us will be at the losing end. They (the advertisers) will be losing half of their audience," said Butch Raquel, corporate affairs director at ABS-CBN.
"It has gotten out of hand. We should sit down and find an amicable solution to this," Raquel added. He could not say, however, if a meeting with the advertisers has been set.
ABS-CBN said its current audience market share is 41 percent.
The dispute over the rates knocked shares of ABS-CBN down by one peso ($0.04) to 30 pesos on volume of 692,600 shares at close of trade on Wednesday, traders said.

Manila brokerage firm Angping & Associates Securities Inc said in its company report on Wednesday that a protracted boycott on ABS-CBN by the country's biggest buyers of airtime will severely affect the company's profits.

"There is room for some concern regarding this move as 80 percent of ABS-CBN's total earnings of 4.3 billion pesos in 1996 came from advertisements," said Jason King, analyst at Angping. The securities firm had a long-term buy on the issue.
ABS-CBN president Eugenio Lopez III said on Tuesday that the company will use increased revenues as a result of the rate increase to finance the station's expansion programme.
